Condensed theatre reference for TruProfile™ implantation only. Not a substitute for the manufacturer IFU or the full SeaSpine® Shoreline® ACS Surgical Technique (D0000975C).

1

Access

Approach the desired level of the anterior cervical spine using the standard ACDF technique.

2

Discectomy & Endplate Preparation

Remove disc material and cartilaginous endplates to prepare the implantation site and create space for the implant.

TIP If the disc space is collapsed, the Disc Wedge can be used as a starter trial to open the space. For a TruProfile construct, use the Plate Template Tool to guide Caspar pin placement — this ensures enough room for the plate once the construct is implanted.
3

Implant Sizing

Select trials for the desired footprint and insert into the disc space to determine implant height. Trials are line-to-line with the interbody; a built-in stop sets the final depth at 1mm sub-flush to the anterior vertebral surface.

TIP Trials are colour-coded by footprint (major colour) and by height (proximal colour band). For a TruProfile construct, the trial's height band identifies the matching plate height and locking cover — see the Implants tab.
4

Implant Selection

Choose the Shoreline® construct for the patient: No-Profile (2-screw, integrated interbody, no plate) or TruProfile™ (2, 3 or 4-screw fixation with plate). Confirm the sterile package tamper seal is intact and the label matches the desired footprint and height before opening — once opened it cannot be returned.

5

TruProfile™ Assembly

Press the plate pins into the holes on the interbody and ensure the plate sits flush.

TIP The Plate Assembly Tool can be used to press the plate firmly onto the interbody.
5

Assembly, continued — Load & Graft Pack

Align the laser-marked lines on the plate with those on the distal end of the Inserter (line-to-line) and turn the knurled knob clockwise until fully engaged — do not over-tighten. Place the construct in the Packing Block and pack the central cavity with graft; the Graft Tamp may be used to pack the material.

6

TruProfile™ Insertion

Ensure the anterior surface has been prepared and any large osteophytes removed. Gently impact the construct into the disc space with a cervical mallet until the plate sits against the spine, then remove the Inserter.

6

Insertion, continued — Remove Inserter & Pins

Turn the knurled Inserter knob counter-clockwise to disengage, then lift the Inserter away. Remove the Caspar pins.

TIP If the plate does not sit flush, check for remaining osteophytes and vertebral body misalignment — in some cases, lagging the screws can help align the vertebral bodies. Fluoroscopy may be used to confirm final positioning.
7

TruProfile™ Screw Preparation

Select the desired guide, awl or drill to create pilot holes. Cranial–caudal angulation: 20° fixed · ±8° variable · 28° max. Medial–lateral (per screw): 10° fixed · ±8° variable · 18° max.

Straight Guide
Variable Guide
Speed Awl · 20° fixed
8

TruProfile™ Screw Placement

Load screws onto the driver by stabbing and grabbing from the caddy. Drive into place using an alternating pattern until fully seated, sub-flush to the plate centre. Use the Straight Screwdriver for best control; the Angled Screwdriver where a straight line is blocked.

9

TruProfile™ Final Locking

With screws snugged sub-flush to the plate centre, select and deliver the height-matched locking cover. Final tighten clockwise with the Locking Cover Torque Handle until the handle clicks — construct complete, torqued to 5 in-lb.

10

Verify Final Implant Position

Using fluoroscopy, verify final Anterior/Posterior and Lateral positioning is satisfactory.

AP view
Lateral view
11

TruProfile™ Closure

Close the surgical site using the standard closure technique required for the procedure.

R

TruProfile™ Implant Removal

Remove the locking cover and screws with the appropriate drivers. Re-engage the Inserter by aligning the laser-marked lines line-to-line and turning the knurled knob clockwise until fully engaged — do not over-tighten. Gently rock the assembly medial-laterally and pull up to remove from the disc space.

TIP If the plate must be separated from the interbody, thread the Plate Removal Tool clockwise into the plate until snug, gently rock cranial–caudally, and pull up to separate it from the interbody.

Tool Set-Up

mini power drill vs hand tools
StageMini Power DrillHand Tools
Set-up12mm drill · straight variable guide · split screwdrivers · charged battery + spareAngled variable guide · straight & angled screwdrivers · AO handle · downforce handle
Pilot holes12mm drill on the mini drill, through the straight variable guideAngled variable guide; 12mm or 14mm drill on the AO handle
ScrewsSplit screwdriver loaded from the caddy, direct to the mini drill — low speedStraight screwdriver for control; angled where a straight line is blocked
🔋
Charge the mini drill battery before the list. Keep a spare charged on the shelf.

Key Instruments

Shoreline® ACS
Plate Assembly Tool (86-1128) — presses the TruProfile plate onto the interbody until flush.
Implant Packing Block (86-0072) — holds the assembled construct while graft is packed into the central cavity.
Angled Drill Guide, Variable (86-0022) — for screw prep where a straight instrument line is blocked.
Angled Drill Guide, Fixed (86-0025) — fixed-trajectory angled screw preparation.
Universal AO Handle (86-9801) — drives hand-tool drills, taps, awls & screwdrivers.
